subject: POC Observability Plan — FintechX (next steps & success criteria)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps (POC observability)

Hi Priya / Aaron,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about FintechX's payment routing use case and the throughput constraints you're seeing during peak settlement windows. As discussed, next step is a short POC focused on latency and correctness under realistic load, with observability built in so your SREs can validate behavior and we can iterate quickly.

I put together a proposed observability plan attached (redwood-poc-observability-plan.pdf). High-level summary:
- Goal: Validate 99th percentile latency <= 300ms on your p95/p99 traffic mix and correctness across 3 representative request patterns.
- Monitoring: token-level latency, request/response traces (end-to-end), model confidence distribution, request sampling + KV cache hit rate, and per-shard GPU utilization.
- Exports: structured logs to your Cloud Logging and a daily metrics dump to the S3 bucket you suggested.
- Dashboards: three dashboards (overview, tail-latency + traces, error/debug). We included a sample dashboard screenshot (sample-dashboard.png).

Suggested timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and test corpus (your 3 flows)
- Week 1: provision POC environment (dedicated sandbox), connect observability exports
- Week 2: run load tests and verification, collect dashboards + traces
- Week 3: review findings and next steps (rollout or tuning)

Ownership proposal:
- Redwood: Jordan (you), Marissa (observability implementation)
- FintechX: Priya (POC owner), Aaron (SRE lead)

Please review the attached plan and the success criteria section in particular. If that looks good, can we lock in Monday 4/26 for the provisioning window?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Thanks — the plan looks reasonable and covers the pieces we care about. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

3) Need to confirm that request logs will not contain PII. We can provide a scrubber on our side but would prefer service-side redaction where possible.

On timeline — Monday 4/26 works for provisioning. Priya here: we'll assign Aaron as our SRE lead (he's cc'd). He'll coordinate network access and our S3 bucket.

Hi Priya / Aaron — thanks for the quick review. Answers below and a couple of clarifications.

1) Traces retention: Redwood will retain full indexed traces for 14 days for the POC (configurable). We can also export archived traces to your S3 bucket on a daily basis if you want longer-term storage.

2) Metrics export: we support Prometheus remote write and time-series exports. For the POC we can push a Prometheus-compatible remote write stream to your metrics endpoint, and also deliver daily aggregated CSVs to S3 if you prefer. Tell us which endpoint you want us to use.

3) PII / log redaction: by default Redwood masks common PII fields in request logs. For anything custom, we can enable a request-side redaction step in the agent you run in your VPC; however, if you prefer, we can accept pre-scrubbed payloads. We'll document the fields we redact in the plan.

Dashboards / widget names: attached in the plan appendix. Key widgets:
- "POC Overview": total requests, successful responses, p50/p95/p99 latency, model confidence histogram
- "Tail Latency & Traces": p99 latency over time, sample trace links, trace waterfall for slow requests
- "Errors & Debug": error by code, sample failed request payloads (redacted)

I'll ask Marissa to lead the implementation of the observability connectors and dashboard provisioning on our side. Marissa — can you take the ownership here and coordinate with Aaron on the metrics endpoint and S3?

Action items:
- Priya/Aaron: confirm Prometheus endpoint URL + S3 bucket and AWS creds for POC (by EOD Thu 4/23)
- Marissa: provision Grafana dashboard templates and remote write config (start Mon 4/26)
- Jordan: run initial smoke tests once provisioning is complete

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks — looping in Sean for infra-level coordination. Quick status update from Redwood observability team:

1) Dashboard templates: I exported Grafana JSON for the three dashboards (overview, tail-latency, errors). I'll push templates to the shared Drive folder and attach the sample screenshots.
2) Remote write: we validated remote write to a Prometheus-compatible endpoint during an internal test. Sean, I'll need vault access to store the write credentials and will send a follow-up with the secret path.
3) Traces: we'll enable 14-day retention and set sampling to 100% for error traces and 1% for normal traffic. We will also export daily batches to S3.
4) Redaction: default masking covers emails and credit-card-like patterns; please send any additional patterns you want redacted and we'll add them to the scrubber config.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Priya/Aaron: share Prometheus endpoint and S3 bucket + IAM role ARN by EOD Thu 4/29 (we need the role for write access)
- Sean: once Marissa shares the Vault path, please grant write-only access to the POC role.
- Jordan: schedule smoke test for Tue 5/3 (tentative)

I'll upload the Grafana JSON and the redaction config to the Drive link in the plan.

Marissa Cole
